releases.summary: Consolidate legacy workflows into the Engineering Skill and add the control-plane checks.
manual_review: Review preserved legacy ramer, fe-engineering, multi-agent, Cursor, and Codex entries before any separate cleanup.

releases.summary: Add approval-bound task DAGs, capability-adaptive parallel execution, deterministic task progress, and Harness-parent/OpenSpec-child orchestration.
manual_review: Active changes created before 0.4.0 must migrate change.json to schema_version 3 with the canonical orchestration contract and add task-plan.json/execution-evidence.json; if already approved, treat the new parent contract and task graph as contract drift and obtain a new external approval before Apply.
Existing approvals that digest tasks.md must be recreated because checkbox progress is now a runtime projection while task-plan.json remains the approval-bound authority.

releases.summary: Adopt OpenSpec 1.12.0 as the lifecycle owner and reduce Engineering to a governance sidecar.
manual_review: Active changes created before 0.5.0 must be reviewed for the retired change.json, task-plan.json, dispatcher, and lifecycle-state files; migrate only after preserving user evidence.
Run `openspec update --force` for existing projects and verify native Skills under the agent-specific directory (Codex uses `.agents/skills`).
Recreate approvals when the OpenSpec schema or tasks.md contract changes; OpenSpec task checkboxes are now the sole progress source.

releases.summary: Expand automatic Engineering Skill discovery and root-entry routing across all supported agent platforms.
manual_review: Verify that the target project has the platform-specific Engineering Skill installed for every supported agent and that its root instruction entry declares automatic routing for non-trivial changes.
Re-run the onboarding check after upgrading so root adapters, platform Skill manifests, and the methodology version are synchronized.

releases.summary: Relocate every Harness resource except openspec/ into a single .hek/ directory.
manual_review: The migration relocates project-owned content: agent-policy.yaml and profile.yaml move to .hek/project/, ai.json and every indexed AI.md move to .hek/context/ (mirroring their module paths), and docs/fitness/ moves wholesale to .hek/fitness/ so project-added checks survive. Review the plan with `hek init --plan` before applying; a destination that already exists is preserved rather than overwritten, and any file edited between plan and apply is kept and reported as kept-modified.

The superseded docs/methodology/ tree is deleted, including files retired before 0.5.0 (templates/, i18n/, examples/ and the Kit's own README/CHANGELOG). Nothing outside that directory is removed automatically.

Add .hek to permissions.writable_paths in agent-policy.yaml. The migration does this for you, but a project that manages the file outside the migration must make the same edit or the control scripts cannot write evidence; the policy is preserved rather than overwritten once it has been filled in.

Rewrite .github/workflows/** by hand. CI triggers and steps that reference docs/fitness/** now need .hek/fitness/**, and .github is deliberately outside the writable paths so the migration never edits it. This is the only reference the migration cannot fix for you.
Update context.index_max_bytes to 8192 and context.detail_max_lines to 800 if the project still carries the pre-0.5.1 limits; check_agent_policy.py fails closed until they match.
References inside openspec/changes/archive/** are intentionally left untouched: they record what was run at the time and rewriting them would falsify the audit trail.
